phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The SG is claimed to have long-range string order in every eigenstate for either boundary condition, whereas without disorder that string order vanishes in many-body eigenstates of free-fermion chains.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Paramagnet-Spin Glass Phase transition
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: At the noninteracting transition, all eigenstates of H_F are claimed to remain localized and H_F is claimed to differ from the canonical strong-disorder-renormalization-group form only by short-range irrelevant terms.

Phase boundaries in the h T1 versus J T2 plane divide the square 0 to pi/2 in each coordinate into PM, 0, pi, and 0pi phases; the 0 and pi regions carry the corresponding edge-Majorana quasienergy modes.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, pi Spin Glass and 0pi Paramagnet, opening paragraph
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: In the localized pi-SG, long-range-ordered cat partners are claimed to be separated by quasienergy pi/T, and the local parity-odd spectral function is claimed to contain a delta-function peak at omega=pi/T.
In the pi-SG, |C_xx| and |C_yy| are claimed to cross exactly twice per period, corresponding to a pi rotation of the SG axis and period doubling.

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: For the free-fermion disordered second drive with open boundaries, the paper reports pi/T edge Majoranas while all other single-particle modes are localized in the bulk.

Disorder-averaged <r> versus J_z for L=8,10,12 under the second drive; the curves support localization for J_z less than or approximately 0.1 and a delocalization crossover/transition around J_z approximately 0.1.

For L=10 and several interaction strengths, the disorder-averaged local spectral function has a pi/T peak in the pi-SG and a zero-frequency peak in the 0-SG at weak interaction, with the peaks disappearing as interaction increases.
For one L=10 interacting pi-phase eigenstate at T1=1 and J_z=0.04, C_xx(L/2;t) and C_yy(L/2;t) exchange dominance through robust within-period crossings.

The 0pi-PM is claimed to have two Majoranas per edge at quasienergies 0 and pi/T, organizing the many-body spectrum into four-state conjugate sets made of two degenerate pairs separated by pi/T; bulk-spin spectral functions are structureless while suitable edge-operator spectra peak at both 0 and pi/T.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The formulas and isolated execution are credible, but the submitted L=6,8 data with only 4-8 samples per point neither reproduce the paper's L=8,10,12 finite-size sequence nor establish the claimed near-critical peak and Poisson tails. The L=8 reduced curve is maximized at the SG endpoint rather than near zero, so the authored science assertion is not backed by its own essential check.

independent_checks.claim: For log-normal variables with unit log standard deviation, the stated standard-deviation identity gives T=pi/W and hence omega=2W, matching the first-drive implementation.
Circular and non-wrapping adjacent-gap conventions differ by at most 0.01145 on the frozen reduced Figure 1 data, so wrap convention alone does not explain the reduced curve.
No paper-scale size, sample, seed, or convergence sweep is present: the frozen run uses L=6,8 with 8 and 4 samples instead of L=8,10,12 with 2000-100000 samples.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The paper's Figure 1 level-statistics claim is false: localized tails do not approach 0.386 and the finite-size peak is not near mean(log J)=mean(log h).
falsification_attempts.method: Compare the frozen reduced curves, their SEMs, and peak locations against the paper statement while refusing to extrapolate from L=6,8 and 4-8 samples.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The reduced data show the expected PM-to-SG contrast and obey the susceptibility bounds, but the paper's asymptotic finite-size claim was not tested at the printed sizes or disorder counts. Qualitative reduced-scale agreement is not a converged reproduction.

independent_checks.claim: The implemented chi_SG includes the i=j contribution and remains in [0,1]; at the PM endpoint L*chi is approximately 1.12 for both L=6 and L=8, consistent with the diagonal 1/L baseline.
At the two reduced endpoints chi_SG rises from 0.187 to 0.954 for L=6 and from 0.139 to 0.916 for L=8, reproducing the qualitative PM/SG contrast.
The bundle has no L=10,12 result, 2000-100000 realization average, independent seed sweep, or finite-size extrapolation for chi_SG.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The paper's claim that chi_SG tends to zero in the PM and remains nonzero in the SG is false.
falsification_attempts.method: Test the endpoint size trend and the exact 1/L diagonal baseline using the frozen reduced data.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: This target is analytic and paper-exact. Independent rederivation gives the two gap-closing lines J T2=h T1 and J T2+h T1=pi/2 on the printed square, and limiting points occupy all four labeled regions with the same orientation as Figure 2(a).

independent_checks.claim: The zero- and pi-gap closings reduce to y=x and x+y=pi/2, which partition the exact [0,pi/2]^2 domain into the four printed sectors.
Independent interior points in the lower, left, right, and upper regions label PM, 0, pi, and 0pi respectively; the frozen 81x81 map contains all four codes and exact boundary arrays.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Figure 2(a) mislabels at least one phase or uses a boundary inconsistent with the binary-drive gap closings.
falsification_attempts.method: Evaluate the two analytic lines and representative limiting points without digitizing the source figure.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The reduced data contain a larger L=8 value near J_z=0.1, but only four samples give a contrast of 1.91 combined SEM and the L=6 maximum occurs at J_z=0.06. The essential check uses an arbitrary difference threshold without convergence or uncertainty significance, and the second-drive duration is not paper-exact.

independent_checks.claim: Circular and non-wrapping gap ratios agree closely on the frozen Figure 2(b) data, excluding the wrap convention as the main cause of the reported crossover.
At J_z=0.1 versus 0.01 the reduced contrasts are only 0.0305 (0.71 combined SEM) for L=6 and 0.0933 (1.91 combined SEM) for L=8; no paper-size or realization convergence is supplied.
The source simultaneously states T=T1+T2, T=1, T2=pi/2, and T1=1; these cannot define one positive-duration drive, and H_x prints an unsummed J_z bond term.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The paper's interaction crossover near J_z approximately 0.1 is false.
falsification_attempts.method: Compare both reduced sizes, SEM-scaled contrasts, peak locations, and circular/non-circular conventions.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The corrected positive Lehmann implementation robustly produces zero/pi peaks and the exact half sum rule, but Equation (7) as printed lacks the absolute square, is eigenvector-gauge dependent, and is generally complex. Because the bundle also uses only L=8, two samples, a reconstructed 0-SG ensemble, an unspecified site/kernel, and an ambiguous duration branch, the strict paper-error-candidate gate is not met; the target remains inconclusive rather than being promoted to a paper error.

independent_checks.claim: With |<alpha|sigma_i^+|beta>|^2 weights, every frozen spectrum is nonnegative and integrates to 0.5 within 1.3e-15, as required by completeness and Tr(sigma^- sigma^+)/2^L=1/2.

The unsquared matrix element printed in Equation (7) changes under independent Floquet-eigenvector rephasing and has literal imaginary RMS 0.0429-0.0446 in the frozen data; therefore it cannot itself define the plotted real positive spectral density.
The submitted spectra use L=8 and two samples per condition rather than the paper's L=10 disorder average, and no kernel/site/ensemble or paper-scale convergence study is frozen.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Equation (7) as printed defines a real, nonnegative, eigenvector-gauge-invariant operator spectral density.
falsification_attempts.method: Rephase a Floquet eigenvector and compare the unsquared matrix element with the absolute-square Lehmann weight; then inspect the frozen literal imaginary RMS and corrected sum rule.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Under the disclosed T1=1, T2=pi/2 branch, the single selected L=8 eigenstate has periodic endpoints and exactly two absolute-correlator crossings. The paper, however, gives mutually incompatible durations and Figure 2(d) uses L=10; one selected reduced eigenstate without seed/branch/size robustness cannot establish the claimed phase-wide robustness or support a strict paper-error finding.

independent_checks.claim: For the frozen chosen branch, C_xx and C_yy return to their initial values within 1.2e-15 and have exactly two absolute-magnitude crossings during the 121-point period.
Combining T=T1+T2 with T=1 and T2=pi/2 gives T1=1-pi/2<0, contradicting both a positive stage duration and the caption's T1=1.
Only one maximally ordered L=8 eigenstate is stored; no L=10 reproduction, second duration branch, seed sweep, eigenstate sweep, or crossing-stability convergence is present.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The printed numerical paragraph, drive equation, and Figure 2(d) caption uniquely specify one positive-duration binary drive.
falsification_attempts.method: Solve the three printed duration statements simultaneously and inspect the H_x interaction index structure.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The authored scope collapses twelve independently inventoried text-level quantitative claims into one generic target. Its twelve machine checks cover runner invariants and selected figure features, not the individually frozen claims about bandwidth hierarchy, long-distance correlators, uniform-chain eigenstate counts, string order, transition eigenstate localization, Majorana/bulk localization, and 0pi four-state pairing. The scope and evidence lifecycle are therefore incomplete.

independent_checks.claim: All eight focused implementation tests pass in the extracted falsification bundle, and the v4 isolated run has return code zero with no forbidden access attempts.

A one-to-one lifecycle invariant fails: the paper-only inventory has six figure items plus twelve distinct text quantitative items, whereas authored scope supplies six figure items plus one aggregate text item.
The generic all-claims target is bound only to reduced data, and no paper-scale run or per-text-claim convergence/evidence record exists.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: T007 and its twelve checks provide complete item-level coverage of every quantitative results-text claim in the paper.
falsification_attempts.method: Compare the frozen paper-only inventory row-by-row with authored numerical_scope_claims and the target IDs attached to each machine check.

findings.claim: The authored scope has one generic Results-text target for twelve independently distinct quantitative text items. Six figure items map one-to-one, but eleven canonical distinctions remain missing even if the aggregate target is assigned to one text row.
reproduction_steps: Read contracts/numerical_scope_claims.json and count six figure rows plus one generic text row.
Enumerate the distinct quantitative claims in paper/paper-source/MBLFloquetSymmetry.tex outside the six plotted subpanels.
Attempt a one-to-one mapping without merging scientific_basis fields; observe that the aggregate authored item cannot cover twelve distinct rows.

findings.claim: Direct cause: the only attested numerical run is reduced scale. Root cause: the paper omits several run choices and the full reconstructed multi-size, multi-million-realization campaign was not executed. Consequently T001, T002, T004, T005, T006, and the numerical parts of T007 lack paper-scale convergence.
reproduction_steps: Inspect the v4 run contract and attestation; verify that the executed configuration is reduced_all_targets.json.
Compare generated row sizes/sample counts with the paper captions' L=8,10,12 and 2000-100000 realization statements.

findings.claim: T001 asserts that both reduced sizes cross between localized and circular-ensemble regimes, but science_checks.json contains no T001-specific peak-location or tail-value check; the L=8 frozen curve is maximized at mean(log J)=3 rather than near zero.
reproduction_steps: List T001-linked checks in machine_evidence/outputs/checks/science_checks.json; only unitarity and family coverage apply.
Find the maximum r_mean for L=8 in generated_data/outputs/data/fig1_observables.json.

findings.claim: Equation (7) prints an unsquared transition amplitude. It is basis-phase dependent and generally complex, while the plotted positive spectral density requires an absolute-square Lehmann weight. The bundle corrects the formula, but paper-exact numeric adjudication is blocked by unspecified kernel/site/normalization and reduced scale.
reproduction_steps: Read Equation (7) in paper/paper-source/MBLFloquetSymmetry.tex and confirm the absence of an absolute square.
Rephase one Floquet eigenvector; observe that the printed amplitude changes phase while its modulus square remains invariant.

findings.claim: The second drive is not uniquely paper-exact: T=T1+T2, T=1, T2=pi/2, and caption T1=1 are mutually incompatible, and the printed H_x interaction term has a free index because the J_z bond sum is missing.
reproduction_steps: Read the drive definition, H_z/H_x equations, numerical paragraph, and Figure 2(d) caption in the source TeX.
Substitute T=1 and T2=pi/2 into T=T1+T2; obtain T1=1-pi/2<0, contradicting the caption T1=1.
Inspect H_x and note that i remains free in the unsummed J_z sigma_i^z sigma_{i+1}^z term.

findings.claim: The v4 reduced run is a genuine isolated execution: return code zero, declared parameters matched, network/subprocess blocked, no forbidden accesses, and frozen output hashes match the falsification bundle. This validates provenance, not paper-scale sufficiency.
reproduction_steps: Inspect the v4 run contract, assurance block, forbidden_access_attempts, and output_files hashes.

findings.claim: T003 is paper-exact and independently supported by analytic boundaries, limiting points, and a four-sector frozen map without source-pixel numerical input.
reproduction_steps: Derive y=x and x+y=pi/2 from the free binary-drive gap closings.
Evaluate representative interior points in each region and inspect the four codes in fig2_phase_diagram.npz.
